judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2) under the same Content Standard B6.2.3.1 (solve problems involving single-variable, one-step equations) within Strand 2 Algebra / Sub-Strand 3 Variables and Equations. B6.2.3.1.2 decomposes into LCs 'Identify the unknown in a problem', 'Represent the problem with an equation' and 'Solve the problem concretely, pictorially or symbolically' — i.e. modelling a given word problem as an equation and solving it. judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 5 Indicators (rank 1, same coordinate) in Strand 2 ALGEBRA but under different Sub-Strands: B5.2.2.1.1 (Sub-Strand 2: Algebraic Expressions) asks pupils to understand algebraic expressions as mathematical phrases containing letters representing numbers and operators, while B5.2.1.1.1 (Sub-Strand 1: Patterns and Relationships, under the Content Standard 'Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements') asks pupils to extend a given pattern with/without concrete materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one. Their LCs (extend a pattern; explain element-to-element difference vs. interpret letters and operators in expressions) are substantively coherent parts of early algebraic reasoning — describing pattern change prepares symbolic description, and expression notation is a tool for pattern rules — but the evidence shows two parallel same-grade sub-strand skills with no stated dependency or sequence, and the nomination's only lexical/code signals ('and', 'of', shared 'b5'/'2' segments, weak rank proximity) are not semantic. Same-rank placement therefore does not supply the substantive evidence needed for a directed buildsTowards, so symmetric coherence is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so absence of an explicit linking exemplar is not conclusive.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicator-grain items at the same resolved coordinate (Grade BASIC 5, rank 1) under the same Algebra / Patterns and Relationships Content Standard B5.2.1.1 ('Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements'), so the grain and topic match and same-rank direction must rest on statement substance rather than shared ancestry, code prefix, or page proximity. The first Indicator (B5.2.1.1.4) asks learners to represent a given pattern visually to verify predictions (LC tags: pattern, predictions, visual representation); the second (B5.2.1.1.7) asks learners to write a rule in words and in algebra to represent a given pattern, decomposed into LCs for a verbal rule and an algebraic rule. Constructing and checking a visual representation of a pattern establishes the structure and verified regularity that a learner must articulate to state that regularity as a generalized verbal and symbolic rule; the second is the more abstract symbolic generalization of the same pattern work, so proficiency in the visual/verification indicator supports success in the rule-writing indicator. Direction is same-rank and grounded on this concrete-to-symbolic abstraction rather than the source ordering .4 before .7. Secure place-value modelling of quantities to 100,000 substantively supports success in computing and solving multi-step whole-number word problems, so a same-rank forward direction from representation to operational problem solving is supported; the reverse is not. The token overlap ('multi') alone is generic and was not treated as the basis. Confidence is moderated because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and the pair spans different sub-strands.
